samples: This program is a command-line tool that reads the numbers you pass as arguments, skips (and reports) any that aren't valid numbers, and then prints their mean, median and population standard deviation, rounded to three decimal places. If no valid numbers are given, each statistic is reported as "no data" rather than failing. It needs only console and environment access, so it does no file or network I/O, and the calculation functions are public, so other code can reuse them.

This program is a command-line tool that reads numbers from its arguments, skips any argument that isn't a valid number (printing a note about each one), and then prints the mean, median and population standard deviation to the console. If no valid numbers are given, each statistic is reported as "no data", and results are rounded to three decimal places. It only needs console and environment access, so it does no file or network activity, and the three calculations are also available as separate public functions you can reuse.
